languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: I adore You devoutly, hidden Godhead,
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: With devotion I adore You, hidden Godhead,

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: who truly lie hidden beneath these forms.
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: who are truly hidden beneath these forms:

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: but by hearing alone one safely believes.
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: but hearing alone gives sure ground for faith:

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: but here the humanity too is hidden at the same time.
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: but here Your humanity is hidden as well.

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: cleanse me, unclean as I am, with Your blood,
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: cleanse me, unclean as I am, with Your blood.

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: one drop of which, to save
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: One saving drop of that blood

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: the whole world from all wickedness, has the power.
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: can free the whole world from every sin.

languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: “Tuto” is taken as the adverb “safely,” so that the safety belongs to believing. The same form could be the ablative of the adjective “tutus” agreeing with “audítu,” “by safe hearing alone,” which makes the hearing itself safe. Either way, faith that rests on hearing is not deceived.
languages/en/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: The adverb “tuto” qualifies “créditur”. The believer can rely on what the Son of God has said. The same form could also be the ablative of the adjective “tutus” agreeing with “audítu”. On that reading, hearing itself is trustworthy.

after.gloss: our life, our sweetness, and our hope

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/benedictio.before: The priest says the first part of the blessing at the altar, then turns to the people and makes the sign of the cross over them. He makes one sign even at a solemn Mass. The threefold blessing belongs to a Pontifical Mass. The blessing is omitted after Benedicámus Dómino and in Masses for the Dead.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/benedictio.after: The priest says the first part of the blessing at the altar, then turns to the people and makes the sign of the cross over them. Even at a solemn Mass, the priest makes this sign only once. The threefold blessing belongs to a Pontifical Mass. The blessing is omitted after Benedicámus Dómino and in Masses for the Dead.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/confiteor-.before: The priest says the Confíteor first, bowed low. He addresses the ministers with “vobis, fratres” and “vos, fratres”. They then make their own confession, saying “tibi, pater” and “te, pater” where he said “vobis, fratres” and “vos, fratres”.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/confiteor-.after: The priest says the Confíteor first, bowed low, and addresses the ministers with “vobis, fratres” and “vos, fratres”. They then make their own confession, saying “tibi, pater” and “te, pater” where he said “vobis, fratres” and “vos, fratres”.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/ecce-agnus.before: The priest shows the Host and points to Christ as the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world. He then says Dómine, non sum dignus three times. He gives the Blessed Sacrament to each communicant with a prayer that the Body of Christ may preserve that person’s soul for eternal life.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/ecce-agnus.after: The priest shows the Host and points to Christ as the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world. After saying Dómine, non sum dignus three times, the priest gives the Blessed Sacrament to each communicant, praying that the Body of Christ may preserve that person’s soul for eternal life.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/evangelium.before: The Prologue of Saint John (John 1:1–14), read at the Gospel side at the end of Mass. Before reading, the priest signs the altar or book and then his forehead, lips, and breast. He genuflects at “Et Verbum caro factum est”.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/evangelium.after: The Prologue of Saint John (John 1:1–14), read at the Gospel side at the end of Mass. Before reading, the priest signs the altar or book and then his forehead, lips, and breast. At “Et Verbum caro factum est”, the priest genuflects.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/fili-dei-v.before: The priest addresses Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God. He recalls the work of salvation accomplished through Christ’s death, by the will of the Father and with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit. He asks to be delivered from iniquity and evil, to remain faithful to the commandments, and never to be separated from Christ.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/fili-dei-v.after: In this prayer to Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, the priest recalls the work of salvation accomplished through Christ’s death, by the will of the Father and with the cooperation of the Holy Spirit. The priest asks Christ to deliver him from iniquity and evil, keep him faithful to the commandments, and never let him be separated from Him.

after.gloss: this most holy Body and Blood of Yours

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/haec-commi.before: The priest drops a small particle of the consecrated Host into the chalice. He quietly asks that this commingling and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ may avail us for eternal life.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/haec-commi.after: The priest drops a small particle of the consecrated Host into the chalice and quietly asks that this commingling and consecration of the Body and Blood of our Lord Jesus Christ may avail us for eternal life.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/hanc-igitu.before: The priest says this prayer secretly, holding his hands spread over the offerings. He asks God to accept this offering, order our days in peace, deliver us from damnation and number us among the elect.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/hanc-igitu.after: Holding his hands spread over the offerings, the priest quietly asks God to accept this offering, order our days in peace, deliver us from damnation and number us among the elect.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/memento-de.before: The commemoration of the dead in the Canon. The priest prays for God’s servants, men and women, who went before with the sign of faith and now sleep the sleep of peace, then joins his hands and prays in silence for those he intends to remember. He asks for them and for all who rest in Christ a place of refreshment, light, and peace.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/memento-de.after: The commemoration of the dead in the Canon. The priest prays for God’s servants, men and women, who went before with the sign of faith and now sleep the sleep of peace, then joins his hands and prays in silence for those he intends to remember. For them and for all who rest in Christ, the priest asks for a place of refreshment, light, and peace.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/per-ipsum..before: This doxology closes the Canon. The priest makes three signs of the cross with the Host over the chalice, then two between himself and the chalice. At omnis honor et glória he slightly raises the chalice with the Host. He says the closing Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum audibly, and the people answer Amen.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/per-ipsum..after: This doxology closes the Canon. The priest makes three signs of the cross with the Host over the chalice, then two between himself and the chalice. At omnis honor et glória he slightly raises the chalice with the Host. The Canon ends with Per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum, which the priest says aloud. The people answer Amen.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/placeat-ti.before: Bowed before the middle of the altar, the priest says this prayer quietly. He asks the Holy Trinity to accept his service and sacrifice and, in mercy, to make it propitiatory for him and for all those for whom it was offered.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/placeat-ti.after: Bowed before the middle of the altar, the priest quietly asks the Holy Trinity to accept his service and sacrifice and, in mercy, to make it propitiatory for him and for all those for whom it was offered.

before.gloss: always and everywhere give thanks to You
He might grant us a share in His divinity

after.gloss: always and everywhere give thanks to You
He might grant us a share in His divinity

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/qui-pridie.before: The institution narrative and the consecration of the bread. The priest takes the Host, raises his eyes to heaven, and pronounces the words of consecration over it quietly, distinctly, and attentively. He then genuflects, shows the consecrated Host to the people, and genuflects again. From this point he does not separate his thumbs and forefingers, except when handling the Host, until the ablution of his fingers.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/qui-pridie.after: The institution narrative and the consecration of the bread. The priest takes the Host, raises his eyes to heaven, and pronounces the words of consecration over it quietly, distinctly, and attentively. After the consecration, the priest genuflects, shows the consecrated Host to the people, and genuflects again. From this point he does not separate his thumbs and forefingers, except when handling the Host, until the ablution of his fingers.

languages/en/texts/ordinarium/suscipe-sa.before: The priest offers the host to God the Father for his own sins, offenses, and negligences, for all who are present, and for all faithful Christians, living and dead. He asks that the offering may avail both him and them unto salvation and eternal life.
languages/en/texts/ordinarium/suscipe-sa.after: The priest offers the host to God the Father for his own sins, offenses, and negligences, for all who are present, and for all faithful Christians, living and dead. In this prayer the priest asks that the offering may bring salvation and eternal life both to him and to them.

after.gloss: my countless sins, offenses, and negligences

languages/en/texts/proprium/commemoratio.before: The sequence Dies irae belongs to all three formularies for the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed. When a priest celebrates the three Masses without interruption, he must say it only at the principal Mass, or at the first Mass if none is principal. He may omit it at the other Masses unless they are sung (1962 Roman Missal, p. 722).
languages/en/texts/proprium/commemoratio.after: The sequence Dies irae belongs to all three formularies for the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed. When a priest celebrates the three Masses without interruption, he must say it only at the principal Mass, or at the first Mass if none is principal. At the other Masses the priest may omit the sequence unless those Masses are sung (1962 Roman Missal, p. 722).

languages/en/texts/proprium/commemoratio.before: At that time, Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews: Everything that the Father gives me will come to me; and the one who comes to me I will not cast out, because I came down from heaven not to do my will, but the will of Him who sent me. And this is the will of Him who sent me, the Father: that of all that He has given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up on the last day. And this is the will of my Father who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him may have eternal life, and I myself will raise him up on the last day.
languages/en/texts/proprium/commemoratio.after: At that time, Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews: Everything that the Father gives Me will come to Me; and the one who comes to Me I will not cast out, because I came down from heaven not to do My will, but the will of Him who sent Me. And this is the will of Him who sent Me, the Father: that of all that He has given Me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up on the last day. And this is the will of My Father who sent Me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him may have eternal life, and I Myself will raise him up on the last day.

after.gloss: with blessed Mary, ever Virgin, interceding

languages/en/texts/proprium/d-n-iesu-chr.before: At that time, Pilate said to Jesus: Are You the King of the Jews? Jesus answered: Are you saying this of yourself, or did others speak to you about me? Pilate answered: Am I a Jew? Your nation and the high priests have handed You over to me. What have You done? Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would surely fight, so that I might not be handed over to the Jews; but now my kingdom is not from here. So Pilate said to Him: Then You are a King? Jesus answered: You say that I am a King. I was born for this, and for this I came into the world, that I may give testimony to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice.
languages/en/texts/proprium/d-n-iesu-chr.after: At that time, Pilate said to Jesus: Are You the King of the Jews? Jesus answered: Are you saying this of yourself, or did others speak to you about Me? Pilate answered: Am I a Jew? Your nation and the high priests have handed You over to me. What have You done? Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world. If My kingdom were of this world, My servants would surely fight, so that I might not be handed over to the Jews; but now My kingdom is not from here. So Pilate said to Him: Then You are a King? Jesus answered: You say that I am a King. I was born for this, and for this I came into the world, that I may give testimony to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice.

languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-res.before: God, today You opened the way to eternity for us through Your Only-Begotten Son, after death had been conquered. You first inspire our desires. Sustain them also with Your help. Through the same Jesus Christ, our Lord, Your Son, who, as God, lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit forever and ever.
languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-res.after: God, today You opened the way to eternity for us through Your only-begotten Son, after death had been conquered. You first inspire our desires. languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-vi-.before: At that time, when a great multitude was with Jesus and they had nothing to eat, He summoned His disciples and said to them: I feel pity for the multitude, because, behold, for three days now they have stayed on with me, and they have nothing to eat; and if I let them go fasting to their homes, they will collapse on the road, for some of them came from far away. And His disciples replied to Him: From where will anyone be able to fill them with bread here in the wilderness? And He asked them: How many loaves do you have? They said: Seven. And He directed the multitude to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves and giving thanks, He broke them and kept giving them to His disciples to serve; and they served them to the multitude. And they had a few small fish; and He blessed them too, and commanded them to be served. And they ate and were filled, and they picked up what remained of the fragments: seven baskets. And those who had eaten numbered about four thousand; and He let them go.
languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-vi-.after: At that time, when a great multitude was with Jesus and they had nothing to eat, He summoned His disciples and said to them: I feel pity for the multitude, because, behold, for three days now they have stayed on with Me, and they have nothing to eat; and if I let them go fasting to their homes, they will collapse on the road, for some of them came from far away. And His disciples replied to Him: From where will anyone be able to fill them with bread here in the wilderness? And He asked them: How many loaves do you have? They said: Seven. And He directed the multitude to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves and giving thanks, He broke them and kept giving them to His disciples to serve; and they served them to the multitude. And they had a few small fish; and He blessed them too, and commanded them to be served. And they ate and were filled, and they picked up what remained of the fragments: seven baskets. And those who had eaten numbered about four thousand; and He let them go.

languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-vii.before: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Be on your guard against false prophets, who come to you in the garments of sheep, but inwardly are rapacious wolves. By their fruits you will know them. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from thistles? So every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit. A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit. Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and cast into the fire. So then, by their fruits you will know them. Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter into the kingdom of heaven; but the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he will enter into the kingdom of heaven.
languages/en/texts/proprium/dominica-vii.after: At that time, Jesus said to His disciples: Be on your guard against false prophets, who come to you in the garments of sheep, but inwardly are rapacious wolves. languages/en/texts/proprium/exaltatio-sa.before: At that time, Jesus said to the crowds of the Jews: Now is the judgment of the world; now the prince of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself. And this He was saying, signifying by what death He was to die. The crowd answered Him: We have heard from the law that the Christ abides forever; and how do You say: The Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man? So Jesus said to them: Yet a little while the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, so that the darkness may not seize you; and he who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may be children of the light.

languages/en/texts/proprium/nativitas-do.before: In many portions and in many ways God spoke of old to the fathers in the prophets; at last, in these days, He has spoken to us in the Son, whom He established as heir of all things, through whom He also made the ages; who, being the splendor of His glory and the form of His substance, and bearing all things by His word of power, making the cleansing of sins, sits on high at the right hand of the Majesty, having been made as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is more distinguished than theirs. For to which of the angels did He ever say: You are my Son, today I have begotten You? And once more: I will be a father to Him, and He will be a son to me? And when He again brings the firstborn into the world, He says: And let all God’s angels adore Him. And concerning the angels He indeed says: Who makes His angels into spirits, and His ministers into a flame of fire. Yet to the Son: O God, Your throne is forever and ever; the rod of Your kingdom is a rod of equity. You have loved justice and hated iniquity; for this reason God, Your God, has anointed You with the oil of exultation above those who share with You. And: You, O Lord, in the beginning founded the earth, and the works of Your hands are the heavens. They will perish, but You will remain; and they will all grow old like a garment, and like a mantle You will change them, and they will be changed; but You are the very same, and Your years will not fail.

languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-ioann.before: At that time, Jesus said to Peter: Follow me. Peter, turning around, saw that disciple whom Jesus loved, following, the one who had also leaned on His breast at the supper and said: Lord, who is it that will betray You? So when Peter had seen him, he said to Jesus: Lord, and this man, what of him? Jesus says to him: Thus I want him to remain until I come; what is that to you? As for you, follow me. So this saying went out among the brothers, that that disciple does not die. And Jesus did not say to him: He does not die; but: Thus I want him to remain until I come; what is that to you? This is that disciple who bears witness of these things and has written these things; and we know that his witness is true.

languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-iosep.before: Beloved by God and by men is he whose memory is blessed. He made him in glory like the saints, and made him great in the dread of his enemies, and by His words He stilled portents. He glorified him before kings, and commanded him in the presence of His people, and showed him His glory. In his faith and gentleness He made him holy, and chose him from all flesh. For He listened to him and to his voice, and led him into the cloud. And He gave him commandments face to face, and a law of life and of instruction.
languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-iosep.after: Beloved by God and by men is he whose memory is blessed. He made him in glory like the saints, and made him great in the dread of his enemies, and at his words God brought the portents to an end. He glorified him before kings, and commanded him in the presence of His people, and showed him His glory. In his faith and gentleness He made him holy, and chose him from all flesh. For He listened to him and to his voice, and led him into the cloud. And He gave him commandments face to face, and a law of life and of instruction.

after.gloss: He brought the portents to an end

languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-iosep.after: In Sirach these are the words of Moses. God brings the signs to an end. The missal leaves the man unnamed in this reading.

languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-matth.before: At that time, Jesus saw a man sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name. And He said to him: Follow me. And rising, he followed Him. And it came to pass, as He was sitting at table in the house, behold, many publicans and sinners came and were sitting at table with Jesus and His disciples. And when the Pharisees saw it, they were saying to His disciples: Why does your Teacher eat with publicans and sinners? But Jesus, hearing it, said: Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. Go, then, and learn what this means: It is mercy I desire, and not sacrifice. For I did not come to call the just, but sinners.

languages/en/texts/proprium/sancti-steph.before: At that time, Jesus was saying to the scribes and Pharisees: Behold, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city, so that there may come upon you all the just blood that was shed on the earth, from the blood of Abel the just to the blood of Zechariah, the son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation. Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who have been sent to you, how often have I willed to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not? languages/pl/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.before: „Tuto” jest tu przysłówkiem i określa samo wierzenie: wiara oparta na słuchu jest bezpieczna. Formę można też odczytać jako ablativus przymiotnika „tutus”, który zgadza się z „audítu”: „samym bezpiecznym słuchem”. Wtedy bezpieczeństwo jest cechą słuchu, przeciwstawionego zwiedzionym zmysłom. Oba odczytania mówią, że wiara oparta na słuchu nie zostaje zwiedziona.
languages/pl/texts/orationes/adoro-te-de.after: Przysłówek „tuto” określa tu czynność wyrażoną przez „créditur”. Wierzący może zaufać słowu Syna Bożego. Druga możliwość to ablativus przymiotnika „tutus”. W tym odczytaniu „tuto” zgadza się z „audítu” i określa słuch jako godny zaufania.

languages/pl/texts/orationes/te-deum.jso.before: Te Deum to starożytny hymn uwielbienia i dziękczynienia. Kościół wyznaje w nim majestat Trójcy Świętej, zwraca się do Chrystusa jako Króla chwały i Sędziego, a następnie błaga o zbawienie, opiekę i miłosierdzie. Polski tekst zachowuje powszechnie znany, dwudziestoośmiowersowy przekład hymniczny ks. Tadeusza Karyłowskiego.
languages/pl/texts/orationes/te-deum.jso.after: Te Deum to starożytny hymn uwielbienia i dziękczynienia. Kościół wyznaje w nim majestat Trójcy Świętej, zwraca się do Chrystusa jako Króla chwały i Sędziego, a następnie błaga o zbawienie, opiekę i miłosierdzie. Polski przekład hymniczny ks. Tadeusza Karyłowskiego przyjęto według Śpiewnika kościelnego Jana Siedleckiego, wydanie jubileuszowe z 1928 r., pieśń 353 (s. 308–309), z modernizacją pisowni i interpunkcji.

languages/pl/texts/proprium/sancti-iosep.before: Miły Bogu i ludziom, którego pamięć jest w błogosławieństwie. W chwale uczynił go podobnym do świętych i wywyższył go ku postrachowi nieprzyjaciół, a słowami swymi uśmierzył groźne znaki. Okrył go chwałą przed obliczem królów, wydał mu rozkazy wobec swego ludu i ukazał mu swoją chwałę. W jego wierze i łagodności uczynił go świętym i wybrał go spośród wszelkiego ciała. Usłyszał go bowiem i jego głos, i wprowadził go w obłok. I dał mu twarzą w twarz przykazania oraz Prawo życia i pouczenia.
languages/pl/texts/proprium/sancti-iosep.after: Miły Bogu i ludziom, którego pamięć jest w błogosławieństwie. W chwale uczynił go podobnym do świętych i wywyższył go ku postrachowi nieprzyjaciół, a na jego słowa Bóg położył kres groźnym znakom. Okrył go chwałą przed obliczem królów, wydał mu rozkazy wobec swego ludu i ukazał mu swoją chwałę. W jego wierze i łagodności uczynił go świętym i wybrał go spośród wszelkiego ciała. Usłyszał go bowiem i jego głos, i wprowadził go w obłok. I dał mu twarzą w twarz przykazania oraz Prawo życia i pouczenia.
W Księdze Syracha chodzi o słowa Mojżesza. To Bóg kładzie kres znakom. W tym czytaniu mszalnym imię Mojżesza zostało pominięte.
